description:
Advances: ancora.derive, ancora.findings

Ready-for: implement

Symptom:
On a real feature branch, mix spec.check reported 39 errors, of which zero describe a contract that actually changed. Builder PR #165 (ChapterSpot/builder, branch feat/builder-xkg-atlas-obo, head 75cbd1fc, Ancora 1.0.0 pinned in mix.lock), CI run 34168086465, verdict line: "checked subjects=50 requirements=578 errors=39 warnings=0 ... spec.check result=fail tier=branch". Breakdown from the log:
- 32 errors are derived/drift (13 subjects x up to 2 functions) plus derived/growth on 13 subjects: builder.usage, builder.solutions, builder.workspaces_sensor, builder.llm_transport, builder.llm_instrumentation, builder.csm_agent, builder.config_editing, builder.agent.tool_error, builder.agent_models, builder.admin_panel, builder.feedback, builder.admin_capabilities, builder.skills. Every one is triggered by the same three bindings: Builder.Sessions.put_active_deploy/4 becoming /5 (a new subject_ref argument), Builder.Sessions.clear_active_deploy/1, and Builder.Agent.CSMAgent.Session.retry_last_async/1. The one subject whose contract those changes belong to, builder.deploy_shepherding, had its spec edited in the same diff and is clean. The other 13 are reached only because the large test files (test/builder/agent/csm_agent_test.exs, test/builder/agent/csm_agent/session_test.exs) carry @tag spec: for many subjects, and their shared setup calls those functions transitively.
- 7 errors are change/uncovered_file on lib/builder/auth.ex, lib/builder/auth/identity.ex, lib/builder_web.ex, lib/builder_web/endpoint.ex, lib/builder_web/router.ex, mix.exs, priv/repo/migrations/20260907195420_add_delegated_identities.exs. Five of those are infrastructure no unit test calls by design. The two auth modules are exercised through the Phoenix pipeline in ConnCase tests, which is exactly the limitation the repo already acknowledges with an overrides entry for builder.auth / derived/unanchored_subject; change/uncovered_file carries no subject ("-" in the log), so no overrides entry can reach it.

Why this is frustrating, stated plainly:
1. The prescribed remedy for drift ("edit the spec for this subject in the same diff") means writing fake requirement edits into 13 spec files whose behavior did not change. An honest implementer refuses, and the gate stays red. The alternative, a Spec-Ack trailer, is documented as "only for a mass mechanical edit whose diff does not change the contract", so using it here means bending the rule the tool wrote.
2. This is the third time the same repo hit the same shape. The builder-9q6 epic recorded it in August 2026 as a ticket-authoring lesson ("multi-mapped files engine.ex, session.ex compel co-changes on subject specs the Allowed list does not name"). Builder PR #164 on 2026-09-07 hit derived/drift on builder.chat_composer_formatting for Sessions.persist_message/3 the same way. Each time an agent spends a review round discovering that the finding is about attribution, not behavior.
3. Every touch of lib/builder/sessions.ex or lib/builder/agent/csm_agent/session.ex will reproduce this, because those modules sit under most subjects footprints. The gate is effectively red-by-default for the two most central files in the app.
4. Infra files (mix.exs, migrations, endpoint, router) can never be covered by a tagged test, so change/uncovered_file is a guaranteed error on any PR that adds a dep or a migration, and the only knob (lib_paths) is too coarse to exclude them without excluding real code.

Evidence:
- CI log: gh run view 34168086465 --repo ChapterSpot/builder --log, job "Checks / Spec Check". Grep for "[ERROR]" and "spec.check result=".
- Categorized extract saved during triage at /tmp/spec165.txt on the monitoring machine (42 lines; 7 uncovered_file, 32 drift+growth across 13 subjects).
- Builder config: .spec/config.yml in ChapterSpot/builder (severities: derived/growth error, change/uncovered_file error; six overrides all for derived/unanchored_subject; no path-level exclusions possible because config only accepts default_base, test_paths, lib_paths, severities, overrides).
- Prior occurrence: bw show builder-9q6 comments dated 2026-08-09 ("TICKET-AUTHORING DEFECTS", item 1) in ChapterSpot/builder.
- Where attribution happens in this repo: lib/ancora/derive/membership.ex and lib/ancora/derive/resolver.ex (footprints follow calls from tagged tests, no notion of a shared helper or a multi-subject test file); lib/ancora/change_analysis.ex:28-38 (uncovered_file is any changed path under lib_paths not in the covered set; no subject, no per-path override).

Why now:
1.2.0 (2026-09-05) added the surface: spec-meta key so drift on non-surface files becomes derived/drift_transitive at info. That addresses part of finding 1 but only when every subject opts in with a surface list, it does nothing for derived/growth on the same subjects, and Builder is still on 1.0.0. Nothing in 1.2.0 touches change/uncovered_file scoping. The Builder OBO work (three PRs, one blocked on this) is the first launch-critical branch to be held by the gate rather than by code, and Manuel has authorized a Spec-Ack trailer on that PR as a temporary bypass, which is exactly the escape hatch the docs say not to use for this.

Suspected cause:
Hypothesis: footprint attribution treats every call reachable from a test tagged to subject S as part of S contract, with no distinction between the function under test and shared setup or fixtures. A per-subject surface list moves the burden onto every spec author; a better default may be to attribute a call to a subject only when it is made from the test body (not setup/describe-level helpers or test/support), or to weight a multi-subject file by which subject tag is nearest the call. Separately, change/uncovered_file needs either a subject so overrides can reach it, or a config list of paths that are declared uncovered by design (migrations, mix.exs, endpoint/router).

## Investigation contract, 2026-09-07

Evidence and corrections:
Report: /Users/mz/Documents/my-vault/LLMs/investigations/ancora/2026-09-07-agent-adoption-friction/04-report.md
Measurements: /Users/mz/Documents/my-vault/LLMs/investigations/ancora/2026-09-07-agent-adoption-friction/03-measurements.md
Source revision: 82c2ca8329e1303ececc610dfc9f72986b96c84a. This contract proposes work; no implementation is claimed.

The historical CI total is verified as 23 drift + 9 growth + 7 uncovered findings, not growth across 13 subjects. Its lock pins 1.0.0. Zero semantic contract changes is unverified. Current default coverage excludes mix.exs and priv/migrations. The measured cause is whole-file union, not production call-graph traversal.

Deliverable:
Correct whole-file attribution. Consume the carrier identity and authored owner mapping from [Tagged-test identity and requirement ownership](https://github.com/iautom8things/ancora/blob/beadwork/issues/ancora-dwf.json). Parse test/support sources into per-side lexical indexes once, then resolve each tagged carrier body plus its applicable setup/setup_all callbacks and statically reachable local or imported test helpers. Include all matching clauses/default arities and bound recursive helper visits with a visited set. Preserve lexical alias/import scope. Stop at production MFAs; do not walk production implementation call graphs. Keep callsite, carrier and helper/callback-chain provenance for explanation. Sibling test bodies and unreachable helper bodies must contribute nothing. Preserve static tag inheritance and generated test carriers without executing generators or macros.

For uncertainty, retain known bindings and existing derived/unresolved_calls disclosures at configured severity, with affected carrier and location. Do not guess unknown calls into coverage. An unresolved helper path must not fabricate shrink: compare proven observations, mark the affected carrier's removal comparison incomplete, and disclose that limitation. Do not retain base bindings as claimed HEAD coverage. Existing parse failures remain errors. Macro injection follows the existing generated-binding companion policy where statically knowable; arbitrary expansion is out of scope.

Apply optional surface ownership consistently to drift, growth and shrink, after [Surface semantics](https://github.com/iautom8things/ancora/blob/beadwork/issues/ancora-8lm.9.json). Retain all bindings. Add derived/growth_transitive and derived/shrink_transitive informational disclosure codes to the closed registry. Partition aggregate set findings by ownership using the applicable base/HEAD defining path. When both surfaces exist, union their declared ownership for this diff; absent HEAD remains conservative; first introduction uses HEAD and is shown as policy change. Unknown defining locations remain primary. Primary configured severities and real shared-setup observations remain intact.

For genuinely uncallable infrastructure inside configured lib_paths, extend existing overrides with an exact file selector for change/uncovered_file and a required reason. File and subject selectors are mutually exclusive; requirement is invalid with file. Initially accept file exceptions at info only, so they remain counted and reviewable; existing explicit global off behavior remains unchanged. Validate canonical project-relative exact paths, no glob/directory exceptions. Show the reason with config provenance. Such a file is excepted, never described as covered. Preserve defaults and library membership. For deleted paths, use base coverage; all remaining paths require HEAD coverage.

Amend the affected contracts/ADR explicitly, including local-helper/import scope changes, footprint provenance, new disclosure codes and file override grammar. Agent guidance must distinguish real contract changes, attribution limitations and intentional policy exceptions. Never prescribe cosmetic requirement edits, test splitting, generated baselines or blanket Spec-Ack as the fix.

Verification:
- Replay the saved alpha/beta fixture through the implemented scanner and full gate: each subject has exactly its own production call plus SharedFixture.prepare/0. Four spurious subject-binding associations disappear. A change only to Beta.value creates zero alpha binding-change/drift findings; an actual Alpha.value change still creates alpha drift. A SharedFixture.prepare change remains observed for both.
- Cover describe/module setup inheritance, named callbacks, reachable local/imported helper chains, default arities, cycles, unused helpers and untagged siblings. Dynamic dispatch stays scoped and disclosed, never claims coverage or proven shrink. Macro/generated observations retain existing positive controls.
- An outside-surface-only binding addition/removal has zero primary growth/shrink findings and one corresponding informational disclosure. Owned additions/removals remain primary. Surface removal cannot demote simultaneous owned changes. No surface is required to benefit from precise attribution.
- Exact lib/router.ex exception changes only that finding to counted config info with its reason; lib/business.ex remains at configured blocking severity. A covered deleted file creates zero fresh uncovered findings, while an uncovered deletion still reports. Retained code losing all HEAD coverage still reports. Default mix.exs and priv/migrations remain outside lib scope.
- Replay saved Builder sources with the corrected implementation and record the before/after subject-binding associations for put_active_deploy and retry_last_async. Direct deploy, csm_agent and tool_error associations in probe.log must survive. Then replay the full historical branch if accessible and classify remaining findings; do not use zero total errors as an acceptance target without semantic review.
- Record consumer parse counts and elapsed time before/after on the same machine and fixtures. Require one parse per test/support file per side and bounded traversal through cycles; investigate material runtime regressions before release.
- After publication, upgrade a consumer once and demonstrate a formerly unrelated-subject failure no longer requires spec/test-layout edits, while a deliberately owned definition change still reports. Publication and this consumer check are required before claiming the fix done.
- Cadence: focused tests during implementation; at final verification run mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix test, mix format --check-formatted, mix deps.unlock --check-unused and mix spec.check against the actual integration base. CI must pass both configured Elixir/OTP combinations. Record evidence of the described symptom after the consuming release before claiming it done.

Allowed touches:
lib/ancora/{derive,tag_scanner,gate,subject_files,change_analysis,config,severity,finding,status,review}.ex and related derive/review modules; focused tests and fixtures; affected derive/parsing/findings/gate/review/scaffold contracts, explicit decision amendments and migration/agent guidance.

Out of Scope (files):
Unrelated production modules, credentials, dependencies and consumer repositories. Release metadata belongs to release preparation.

Out of Scope (intent):
No semantic-equivalence claim, production call-graph traversal, target test execution from Ancora tasks, disk baseline, mandatory manual binding inventory, consumer fake spec edits, global coverage disablement or unrelated performance work.

Merge gate:
- [ ] Focused negative and positive behavior fixtures pass.
- [ ] Affected specs and decisions describe the actual changed behavior.
- [ ] Full repository CI and spec gate pass without cosmetic acknowledgment edits.

Decision:
Choose per-test reachability plus explicit narrow policy. Whole-file resolution adds measured sibling and unused-helper associations. Surface-only and policy-only approaches cannot remove those associations. Keep real setup observations and uncovered-code checks; reuse reasoned overrides for the exact infrastructure limitation.

Open Questions:
None. Unmeasured consumer replay and release behavior are explicit Verification obligations, not claimed results.

comments.text: Investigated. Choose per-test attribution with preserved setup/helper observations, consistent optional surface classification, and exact reasoned infrastructure exceptions. Six implementation contracts recorded; no source implementation claimed. Historical count corrected to 23 drift, 9 growth, 7 uncovered on Ancora 1.0.0. title: spec.check fans drift/growth across unrelated subjects and flags untestable infra files, with no way to scope either
